Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office province; the deed is executed by a Notario and filed electronically via CIRCE / Ventanilla Única Empresarial.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Articles 1, 2, 20-23, 58, 62, 66, 175-178, 209-216 and 231); supplemented by Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores (electronic incorporation via CIRCE and optional Formación Sucesiva SL with EUR 1 capital).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) with adopted estatutos sociales, submitted for mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 45 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

SL minimum share capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash before deed execution, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) issued by a Spanish credit institution and annexed to the public deed; the funds remain blocked until registration. Alternative regime: Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva under Ley 14/2013 with EUR 1 capital but subject to dividend restrictions, minimum legal reserve obligations, and dissolution triggers; standard ES_SL template applies EUR 3,000 paid-up capital.

Funding & unlock path: No civil-defense structural or industrial load permits apply to the platform activity, which is hosted on cloud infrastructure. For any leased office or esports venue, obtain: (1) fire-safety compliance certificate under CTE DB-SI and periodic inspections per RIPCI; (2) occupancy-load clearance for public tournament areas; and (3) a workplace risk assessment and prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including ergonomic workstation evaluations, first-aid provisions, and appointment of a prevention officer where employee thresholds are met.

Paid-in capital rule: SL minimum share capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash before deed execution, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) issued by a Spanish credit institution and annexed to the public deed; the funds remain blocked until registration. Alternative regime: Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva under Ley 14/2013 with EUR 1 capital but subject to dividend restrictions, minimum legal reserve obligations, and dissolution triggers; standard ES_SL template applies EUR 3,000 paid-up capital.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
FIRST: The incorporation deed and articles of association having been executed and approved, all capital subscriptions of EUR 3,000, fully paid in, are ratified; the administrator is directed to complete Commercial Registry registration and convert the provisional tax code. SECOND: The registered office is fixed at Calle Gran Vía 42, Planta 3, 28013 Madrid, Spain, within the Madrid commercial registry district; management may relocate offices within the same province without an extraordinary resolution. THIRD: [Full Name] is appointed Sole Administrator with full powers to open and operate bank accounts, appoint agents, sign membership and payment-rail agreements, and procure the esports, data-protection and municipal licenses for the business. FOURTH: All governmental filings incidental to incorporation are ratified.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing, warehouse, or physical production installation. If a physical office, esports venue, or public-event facility is opened: Ayuntamiento de Madrid — Área de Gobierno de Obras y Equipamientos / Oficina de Licencias through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial, with regional oversight by the Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo de la Comunidad de Madrid for public esports events.

Category: No mandatory operating permit for the pure digital esports matchmaking and tournament platform (ISIC 5820 / CNAE 5820). For any leased premises or intermittent tournament venue, the applicable authorization is the municipal Licencia de Apertura or, for lower-impact premises, the Declaración Responsable de Actividad; public esports tournaments with spectators require the Licencia de Espectáculos Públicos y Actividades Recreativas of the Autonomous Community of Madrid.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es (Sede Electrónica).

E-government filing portal

Spanish SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada): (1) obtain negative name certificate from Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute public deed before a notary; (3) file Model 036 with AEAT to request the provisional NIF (format B-XXXXXXXX); (4) register the company in the Registro Mercantil within the legal term; (5) obtain the definitive NIF and the statistical card (tarjeta estadística). Foreign enterprises without a permanent establishment but with taxable supplies in Spain must obtain an NIF for non-residents by filing Model 036 through a tax representative, attaching apostilled constitutional documents and a certificate of residence of the foreign entity.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SL is a fully tax-transparent entity; resident SLs are subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at the 25% headline rate (23%/21% reduced SME rate for tax periods 2023-2024/2025+ where net turnover < €1M; 15% reduced rate for newly created entities in year 1-2 if the activity is not subject to an undistributed profits reserve limitation). Non-resident shareholders are subject to non-resident income tax (IRNR) on distributions and capital gains; Spain applies the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 0% withholding rate for qualifying corporate shareholders. Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for resident companies, with foreign tax credit; the SL can opt for tax consolidation under Article 64 LIS once the 70%/75% group participation test is met. — Spanish SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada): (1) obtain negative name certificate from Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute public deed before a notary; (3) file Model 036 with AEAT to request the provisional NIF (format B-XXXXXXXX); (4) register the company in the Registro Mercantil within the legal term; (5) obtain the definitive NIF and the statistical card (tarjeta estadística). Foreign enterprises without a permanent establishment but with taxable supplies in Spain must obtain an NIF for non-residents by filing Model 036 through a tax representative, attaching apostilled constitutional documents and a certificate of residence of the foreign entity.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation: the SL is a fully tax-transparent entity; resident SLs are subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at the 25% headline rate (23%/21% reduced SME rate for tax periods 2023-2024/2025+ where net turnover < €1M; 15% reduced rate for newly created entities in year 1-2 if the activity is not subject to an undistributed profits reserve limitation). Non-resident shareholders are subject to non-resident income tax (IRNR) on distributions and capital gains; Spain applies the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 0% withholding rate for qualifying corporate shareholders. Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for resident companies, with foreign tax credit; the SL can opt for tax consolidation under Article 64 LIS once the 70%/75% group participation test is met.

Available election forms

Spain operates no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is fixed by the corporate form (LIS Article 8). Available elections include: (i) tax consolidation group regrouping (Art. 64-67 LIS) upon prior communication to AEAT; (ii) application of the special VAT simplified scheme (Model 037) and agriculture/forestry/livestock scheme where turnover ceilings are met; (iii) the Union One-Stop Shop (OSS) non-Union OSS and Import OSS schemes for distance sales and B2C digital services; (iv) accelerated R&D&I tax credits (Art. 35 LIS); (v) the Patent Box regime (Art. 23 LIS) for qualifying IP; (vi) Spanish non-resident tax registration designations (PE vs. isolated operation vs. Art. 12.5 IRNR seizure election); and (vii) reversal of the burden of the anti-hybrid rules of Art. 15.f) and 62 LIS under ATAD transposition (Law 22/2021), requiring taxpayers to pre-emptively disclose hybrid mismatch outcomes in Model 023 (cross-border arrangements, DAC6) where materialized.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general de-minimis exemption threshold: any taxable person habitually carrying out taxable economic activities in Spanish territory must apply for a VAT number (NIF-IVA, followed by the ES prefix for intra-EU) before starting the activity via Model 036/037. For the optional simplified scheme (régimen simplificado) eligibility, prior-year net turnover must not exceed €250,000 for goods resale or €125,000 for services; for distance sales into Spain, the intra-EU distance-selling threshold is €10,000 (unionwide OSS option).

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of tangible goods to non-EU destinations are exempt with credit (0% VAT) under Art. 21.1 LIVA, provided the goods leave the EU customs territory; the export must be evidenced and the dispatch must occur within 90 days of the invoiced supply (Art. 22 LIVA; extension permitted by customs). Digital and esports platform services: B2B cross-border supplies to non-EU or EU customers follow the B2B place-of-supply rule (customer establishment), so Spanish VAT is not levied/reverse-charged; for B2C remote digital services to final consumers in other Member States, the Union OSS regime allows the platform to self-assess the destination-country VAT (Spanish standard rate 21%), while supplies to non-EU consumers fall outside Spanish VAT entirely; the sale of physical merchandising exported from Spain to non-EU customers qualifies for the Art. 21 export exemption. The exporter must have obtained the customs export declaration (DUA/EX) and dispose of the goods at the time of departure.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD — Documento Único Administrativo) XOR ECS electronic export summary declaration
  • Proof of exit: customs stamp, Sortie Certificate, or in-house computer check (E-portal) under Art. 795 of EU Reg. 2015/2447
  • Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill or equivalent transport title that unequivocally evidences the non-EU destination
  • Commercial invoice and proforma export contract
  • Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT credit advice showing collection of the foreign-exchange proceeds
  • Banking settlement and repatriation statements (Model 036/declaración informativa de operaciones con el exterior) for exchange-control evidence
  • Internal movement records (ALLE-DOT) if the dispatch is made from bonded warehouses

Real-time/incremental fiscal clearance is implemented through two systems: (i) SII — Suministro Inmediato de Información (RD 596/2016; effective since 2017): obliged businesses (>€6M turnover, VAT groups, foreign registration category 151, etc.) must upload invoice records to AEAT within 4 calendar days (8 days for certain records and amendments) in XML schema 3.1; (ii) Verifactu (RD 1007/2023, mandatory for all billing software at issuer level from April 2025 and compulsory as business accounting support from April 2026): requires software suppliers to obtain a verifiable declaration of conformity, QR codes and digital traceability for each invoice. Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) mandates B2B e-invoicing exchange on a state digital invoice platform (solution available as of 2024; mandatory within one/two-year deadline by company size depending on regulation date). Non-compliance carries the penalties of Ley 58/2003 (LGT) and specific SII-formalities penalties up to €10,000 per omission.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The euro is fully convertible; Spain maintains no exchange controls. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are liberalized under EU Treaty provisions (TFEU Articles 63-66) and Spanish Law 19/2003 on capital movements. Profit remittance by an SL is unrestricted subject only to corporate tax compliance, certification of non-domiciled payment flows, and standard AML documentation; no prior administrative authorization is required.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Spain. Exporters and providers of digital services may freely retain foreign currency proceeds in resident or non-resident bank accounts, with no timeline or repatriation deadline, though receipts must be booked for balance-of-payments reporting when they affect Spain's international investment position.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); foreign exchange administration is jointly executed with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMEX) under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise (Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa) for investment declarations and balance-of-payments statistics.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium-to-High for EU/EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passporting into Spain under PSD2 and the EBA passport regime (e.g., N26, Qonto, Berkay); these can provide SEPA and SWIFT rails with fully compliant Spanish IBANs. Offshore non-EU EMIs and unlicensed neobanks are Low viability and effectively barred from offering payment accounts to an ES_SL without a Spanish or EEA license due to Banco de España registration requirements and AML Law 10/2010 restrictions.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Opaque UBO structure where esports tournament prize flows involve global players or aggregator payment wallets without clear identification of final beneficiaries.

Root cause: Opaque UBO structure where esports tournament prize flows involve global players or aggregator payment wallets without clear identification of final beneficiaries.

Defense evidence: Certified UBO registry extract (Registro de Titularidades Reales), notarized organizational chart, passport copies of all natural-person UBOs, corporate register certificate (Certificación del Registro Mercantil), and a written description of the tournament prize pool custody and disbursement flow.
High-risk source-of-funds concentration from crypto-currency prize payouts or gambling-adjacent jurisdictions flagged by bank sanctions screening.

Root cause: High-risk source-of-funds concentration from crypto-currency prize payouts or gambling-adjacent jurisdictions flagged by bank sanctions screening.

Defense evidence: Independent audit of platform wallet balances, transactional ledger history tracing inbound funds to identifiable commercial counterparties, player-payout policy governing taxes and chargebacks, exchange/wallet provider license evidence, and confirmation that the platform does not involve regulated gambling services.
Cross-border revenue concentration from Latin American markets triggering enhanced transfer and corresponder-bank scrutiny.

Root cause: Cross-border revenue concentration from Latin American markets triggering enhanced transfer and corresponder-bank scrutiny.

Defense evidence: Executed commercial agreements with LatAm distribution partners, transfer pricing documentation (Form 232 and Chapter VI OECD TP report if applicable), customer and counterparty KYC files, bank statements of related collection entities, and a treasury management policy demonstrating upstream tax withholdings and intercompany loan/fee governance.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Equity or shareholder loan injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank) to the ES_SL's euro-denominated operational account quoting purpose code 1010-capital subscription (or 1120-loans) under the Bank of Spain Balance of Payments classification; the foreign investment must be reported post-investment through DGCOMEX Form D-1A if the non-resident investor holds at least 10% or the transaction exceeds EUR 3,000,000, with the SL's NIE tax ID and registered address validated before credit confirmation.International disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for direct correspondent-bank payments to non-EU suppliers and SEPA CT (ISO 20022 pain.001) for EU/EEA counterparts; for high-value esports tournament licensing or strategic acquisitions, irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit and standby credits are issued through Santander/CaixaBank trade desks, while LatAm collections may be consolidated via treasury pooling and cleared through SWIFT or local clearing systems (e.g., SPEI in Mexico) with NDF coverage.Outright EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm currency forwards (deliverable) with authorized Spanish credit entitiesNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies such as ARS, COP, and VES where physical settlement is prohibitedCross-currency swaps (EUR vs USD/GBP) for hedging long-term intercompany loan or tournament guarantee exposuresVanilla FX options (EUR calls/puts) for asymmetric mitigation on tournament prize pools and licensing milestone receipts

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium-to-High for EU/EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passporting into Spain under PSD2 and the EBA passport regime (e.g., N26, Qonto, Berkay); these can provide SEPA and SWIFT rails with fully compliant Spanish IBANs. Offshore non-EU EMIs and unlicensed neobanks are Low viability and effectively barred from offering payment accounts to an ES_SL without a Spanish or EEA license due to Banco de España registration requirements and AML Law 10/2010 restrictions.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% statutory withholding on dividends, profit distributions and participation in profits paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder without a Spanish permanent establishment (Art. 25.1 of RDL 5/2004, Non-Resident Income Tax Law). The 19% rate also applies where the distribution is made through an intermediary account holder.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the tax year-end. For a calendar-year SL, filing must be completed by 25 July of the following year. A different fiscal year may be adopted only if expressly provided in the bylaws; the deadline then runs from that fiscal year-end.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Due by the 20th day of April, October and December respectively for the 3-month, 6-month and 9-month periods ending on 31 March, 30 September and 30 November; for a calendar-year taxpayer the instalment calendar is 20 April, 20 October and 20 December.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 00001 NIF - Spanish tax identification number of the legal entity (format A/B/C/J followed by eight digits, with control letter). A non-resident entity acting through a Spanish permanent establishment must use the PE's own NIF; a foreign parent NIF is not accepted. A non-resident without a PE is outside Form 200 and files Form 210 instead. Voluntary late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers a progressive surcharge under Art. 27 LGT of 5% of tax due within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. Compulsory late filing after AEAT notice attracts fixed penalties under Art. 198 LGT of EUR 150 to EUR 1,500, or, if collection is affected, 2% of the relevant tax amount. Substantial underdeclaration is penalised at 50% to 150% of the evaded tax under Art. 191 LGT. Loss of Form 200 filing rights may invalidate loss offsets and tax credits.

The PE must adopt the same fiscal year as its foreign head office where the head office's accounting period is used for Spanish bookkeeping; otherwise calendar-year convention applies. Box 00556 Capitalization reserve reduction under Art. 25 LIS, limited to the smaller of 10% of the increase in net equity and 10% of the taxable base. The reserve is likewise available to a PE only if the foreign entity records the equivalent reserve in its head-office accounts and meets the equity maintenance test. Box 00561 Offset of prior-year negative taxable bases (compensacion de bases imponibles negativas), mandatorily declared in the order of generation. PEs may only offset negative bases previously computed in the same Spanish PE; losses are not transferable from the head office or other group entities. PEs include Spanish withholdings suffered on interest, dividends and royalties sourced in Spain; foreign tax credits are not entered here. Box 00598 Differential result (cuota diferencial): the final amount payable to the AEAT or refundable to the taxpayer. Payment must be made in euros from a Spanish bank account; refunds are remitted to the PE's Spanish account or to the foreign head office upon request. Box 01 NIF of the entity making the instalment payment. A PE uses its Spanish PE NIF; instalments are computed only on the PE's Spanish results. Late or omitted instalments accrue late-payment interest and are offset by the AEAT against the final annual assessment. The progressive surcharge and penalties of Art. 27 and Art. 198 LGT apply as for the annual return; deliberate understatement attracts the 50% to 150% penalty of Art. 191 LGT on the underpaid instalment.
Box 02 Tax period of the current return and the month covered by the instalment. The PE follows the same tax period as the head office where possible; otherwise calendar-year intervals apply. Late or omitted instalments accrue late-payment interest and are offset by the AEAT against the final annual assessment. The progressive surcharge and penalties of Art. 27 and Art. 198 LGT apply as for the annual return; deliberate understatement attracts the 50% to 150% penalty of Art. 191 LGT on the underpaid instalment.
Box 20 Calculation base under the method elected in Art. 40.3 LIS: either the final corporate tax liability (cuota integra) of the preceding tax period, or the accounting profit accrued from the first day of the tax period to the day immediately preceding the instalment deadline. PEs use the PE-specific preceding-year liability or the PE's own accrued accounting profit; the method must be consistent for all instalments of the year. Late or omitted instalments accrue late-payment interest and are offset by the AEAT against the final annual assessment. The progressive surcharge and penalties of Art. 27 and Art. 198 LGT apply as for the annual return; deliberate understatement attracts the 50% to 150% penalty of Art. 191 LGT on the underpaid instalment.
Box 29 Percentage applied to the base: 20% when using the prior-year cuota integra method; 17% of the year-to-date accounting profit for entities with annual turnover below EUR 10 million; 0% for newly created entities during the first two tax periods. PEs are generally excluded from the 0% option and apply the standard 17% or 20% percentages. Late or omitted instalments accrue late-payment interest and are offset by the AEAT against the final annual assessment. The progressive surcharge and penalties of Art. 27 and Art. 198 LGT apply as for the annual return; deliberate understatement attracts the 50% to 150% penalty of Art. 191 LGT on the underpaid instalment.
Box 93 Amount to pay to the AEAT, net of withholdings and of instalments already paid earlier in the same year. Payment must be made by SEPA direct debit or electronic transfer; underpayment generates late-payment interest from the original instalment due date. Late or omitted instalments accrue late-payment interest and are offset by the AEAT against the final annual assessment. The progressive surcharge and penalties of Art. 27 and Art. 198 LGT apply as for the annual return; deliberate understatement attracts the 50% to 150% penalty of Art. 191 LGT on the underpaid instalment.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 250,000 aggregate related-party transactions in a tax period triggers mandatory preparation and filing of the Local File (documentacion especifica) and of the Modelo 232 informative return; a Master File (documentacion maestra) is additionally required for groups whose consolidated revenue for the preceding tax period equals or exceeds EUR 45,000,000. Related-party transactions with a single related party exceeding EUR 100,000 in respect of royalties, interest, insurance premiums and certain service categories also trigger Modelo 232 reporting.
